title: claimspec v1 — sweep
description: What a sweep proposed and what survived it. A sweep probes faults NOBODY STATED: it takes the changed source files that carry no claim, proposes faults with the mechanical producers, and reports the ones a green suite did not notice. Its findings are therefore weaker evidence than a probe's — no human said the behaviour mattered — and stronger than nothing, which is what a repository with no claims has. The drafts it carries are proposals for a human to keep or drop; they are not claims, and nothing here belongs in a claims file until someone states the sentence it defends.

ref.description: The reference the change was measured against.

mode.description: What the sweep was pointed at. `changed` proposes for the changed source files that carry no claim. `save-paths` proposes for every file that writes to storage, because a diff cannot answer how many save paths exist — and a clean report over an unstated denominator is a sample of unknown size, not a guarantee.

changed.description: Files in the change, before any filter.

targets.description: Changed SOURCE files carrying no claim — what the gate calls uncovered. A sweep proposes against these and nothing else.

swept.description: Targets that yielded at least one proposal. Never more than `targets`: a file the producers cannot touch is skipped, not swept.

skipped.description: Targets that produced nothing, and why. Recorded rather than dropped: a file that silently yielded no proposal reads as a file with no findings.

writeSites.description: save-paths only: calls that write to storage across the whole surface, not only the ones probed.

payloadFields.description: save-paths only: payload keys sitting on their own line, which is what a field-dropped fault can anchor to.

selection.description: What was proposed and what was probed. A sweep is capped — past a few findings per file nobody reads them, and the runner is spent either way — so the count NOT probed is reported beside the count that was. A cap that hides its own remainder is a coverage claim nobody made.

deferred.description: Proposed and not probed. Not a verdict of any kind.

byClass.description: Per fault class: how many were proposed, how many probed, and how many sat on a write payload.

counts.description: Every verdict the probe reached, including `killed`. A sweep whose faults were all caught is a real result and must be readable as one.

findings.description: Every record that was not killed, most actionable first. `survived` and `nocover` are statements about the test suite; the rest are statements about the PROPOSAL and do not gate, because a sweep's faults are machine-made and a tool that fails on its own bad guess gets switched off.

writePath.description: The fault sits on a database write or the payload of one. Every surviving fault in the measurement that prompted this field was such a line.

hint.description: One line naming the mechanism, never only the verdict.

signals.description: Static, annotation-grade signals about the defenders of a SURVIVOR on the write path. They never change a verdict. `persistence-payload-unasserted`: the defender mocks the persistence layer and the file's call assertions never name an exact payload, so a field dropped from a write cannot fail them. Descriptive, never predictive: no threshold on the assertion mix separates the files whose payload faults survive from the files whose do not.

drafts.description: The draft claims documents the proposals came from, carried so a human can keep one without re-running the sweep. Drafts, never claims: every statement is a TODO nobody has written yet.
